---
title: "PM2 deployment"
description: "Generate an optional PM2 ecosystem file and reload only the current application."
---

`warlock pm2 init` writes `ecosystem.config.cjs` from your app and build
configuration. PM2 is optional operator tooling: core neither installs nor imports
it. Install PM2 separately on the deployment host and put its CLI on `PATH`.
Use Node 22.15 or newer for both the app and the PM2 daemon; cluster workers use
the daemon's Node runtime.

```bash
NODE_ENV=production npx warlock build
NODE_ENV=production npx warlock pm2 init
# Review the generated file and its exact app name before starting it.
pm2 start ecosystem.config.cjs --only store-api-production

# After deploying another successful build:
NODE_ENV=production npx warlock pm2 reload
# Or reload just one verified worker:
NODE_ENV=production npx warlock pm2 reload --id 7
```

Here `package.json` has `"name": "store"` and `src/config/app.ts` exports
`{ appName: "api" }`. Run these commands from the app root using the same
`NODE_ENV` and identity overrides every time. Config modules are evaluated;
bootstrap, prestart and connectors are not run by this command.

## Identity and generated settings

The name is `<project>-<app>-<env>`:

| Part    | Source                                                                         |
| ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| project | `--project`, otherwise `package.json` name; `@team/store` becomes `team-store` |
| app     | `--app`, otherwise `app.appName`, otherwise `app`                              |
| env     | `NODE_ENV`, otherwise `development`                                            |

Choose a project/app combination unique within your PM2 daemon. Components must
start with a letter or digit and contain only letters, digits, `_` or `-`.
Display names containing spaces need a safe `--app` override. No regular
expressions, comma lists, selectors or arbitrary name flags are accepted.

| Setting               | Value                                                                          |
| --------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `cwd`                 | Absolute app root                                                              |
| `script`              | Resolved `build.outdir` / `build.outDirectory` + `build.outFile`               |
| `interpreter`         | Node executable used for generation                                            |
| `node_args`           | `--enable-source-maps` unless `build.sourcemap` is `false`                     |
| `exec_mode`           | `fork`; `--cluster` selects `cluster`                                          |
| `instances`           | `1` in fork mode; `2` with `--cluster`; override with `--instances 3` or `max` |
| `wait_ready`          | `true`                                                                         |
| `listen_timeout`      | `30000` ms; override with `--listen-timeout 60000`                             |
| `kill_timeout`        | `app.shutdownTimeout`, default `10000` ms                                      |
| `env.NODE_ENV`        | Environment used during generation                                             |
| `time` / `merge_logs` | `false`, preserving logger timestamps and per-worker log files                 |

`init` works before a build exists and without PM2 installed. It refuses to
overwrite an existing ecosystem file. Review or move the old file before
generating a replacement. The generated file contains only the selected runtime
settings, not the rest of the app configuration or its secrets. Regenerate it
when build paths, app identity, timeouts or environment change; `reload` uses
the settings already registered in PM2 and does not apply edits to this file.

## Readiness and shutdown

The generated file runs the bundle directly. Pointing PM2 at `warlock start`
would supervise a second supervisor instead of the process that owns HTTP.
Rebuild with core 5.33.0 or newer to include the PM2 readiness signal.

At completed boot, after early and late connectors (including the HTTP listener
and configured socket adapter) have finished, core sends `process.send("ready")`
when an IPC channel and PM2's `pm_id` are present. Socket-only apps also await
their listener and reject bind failures before readiness. It sends once and keeps PM2's
channel open. `warlock start` retains its separate versioned handshake; a plain
Node launch without IPC sends nothing.

PM2's [`wait_ready` and timeout semantics](https://pm2.keymetrics.io/docs/usage/signals-clean-restart/)
define the deployment budget: `listen_timeout` bounds the wait for readiness;
`kill_timeout` bounds the time from the shutdown signal to a forced kill. PM2
sends `SIGINT` by default, which core handles with graceful shutdown. A timeout
can force a reload/restart despite missing readiness, so choose a readiness
budget above your observed cold boot time and use an external deployment probe.
The IPC message reports completed boot, not continuously healthy dependencies.

The generated comment and CLI output give the configured `/ready` URL, respecting
host, port, TLS and `http.health.readinessPath`. Wildcard hosts become loopback
addresses for local probes. HTTP disabled, health disabled or port `0` produces
an explicit unavailable notice. PM2 does not poll this URL automatically.

`kill_timeout` matches core's overall connector budget, `app.shutdownTimeout`,
rather than PM2's short default. Keep HTTP draining below that budget, with
room for other connectors, app shutdown hooks and log flushing:

```ts title="src/config/app.ts"
import type { AppConfigurations } from "@warlock.js/core";

export default {
  appName: "api",
  shutdownTimeout: 20000,
} satisfies AppConfigurations;
```

Set `http.gracefulShutdown.timeout: 10000` in `src/config/http.ts` for this
example. Core's connector timer starts after app shutdown hooks and finishes
before the final log flush; PM2's budget covers the entire process exit, so slow
hooks or flushes can consume its allowance. See [Health checks](../digging-deeper/health-checks.md).

## Rolling reloads and sockets

```bash
NODE_ENV=production npx warlock pm2 init --cluster --instances 2
```

PM2's [cluster reload](https://pm2.keymetrics.io/docs/usage/cluster-mode/) replaces
workers while other workers keep serving. Fork mode falls back to a restart
and can interrupt requests; the CLI prints that limitation. Reload refuses
cluster workers that are offline or lack `wait_ready: true`. PM2 can still fall
back on timeout, so zero downtime depends on successful boot and draining.

Store sessions and shared state outside individual workers. Each worker also
runs app initialization and any enabled worker tasks; separate your worker
deployment or coordinate scheduled jobs so they do not run once per HTTP worker.

With a socket configuration present, cluster generation and reload require:

- A `socket.adapter` factory for cross-worker broadcasts, such as the Redis
  adapter described in [Sockets](../digging-deeper/socket.md#multiple-servers).
- `socket.options.transports: ["websocket"]`, with WebSocket-only clients.

Core refuses sockets without an adapter, even if the single-server warning is
silenced. It also refuses polling in this generated cluster setup: affinity to
a shared PM2 port cannot select its individual workers. If you need polling,
run distinct fork listeners behind sticky routing to those listeners, or arrange
a custom cluster primary with worker affinity. An adapter alone does not provide
sticky sessions. See the official [Socket.IO multi-node guide](https://socket.io/docs/v4/using-multiple-nodes/).

## Shared-server operations

`warlock pm2 reload` reads `pm2 jlist`, matches the exact generated name, and
verifies every target's absolute working directory and bundle path before
reloading anything. It then invokes `pm2 reload <numeric-id>` sequentially.
`--id` narrows this to one worker and still verifies ownership. A conflicting
same-name process causes refusal; a missing or invalid build-success marker
also refuses reload. PM2 must already be installed and the ecosystem started.

For stopping an app on a shared daemon, inspect its **current** PM2 ids and
paths first, then stop only the intended id (repeat for each owned worker):

```bash
pm2 list
pm2 show 7
pm2 stop 7
```

A PM2 id is not an OS PID. Recheck it after deleting/recreating an app. Avoid
name/pattern stops, `all`, and ecosystem-wide stop/delete operations on shared
servers. PM2 documents [process management](https://pm2.keymetrics.io/docs/usage/process-management/)
and [ecosystem selection](https://pm2.keymetrics.io/docs/usage/application-declaration/).
The `.config.cjs` extension is supported in PM2's
[configuration loader](https://github.com/Unitech/pm2/blob/master/lib/Common.js).

## Logger output

PM2 captures stdout/stderr; it does not convert those lines into
`@warlock.js/logger` entries. Configure a terminal channel in production if you
want app logs in PM2:

```ts title="src/config/log.ts"
import { ConsoleLog } from "@warlock.js/logger";

export default {
  production: { channels: [new ConsoleLog({ showContext: true })] },
};
```

`ConsoleLog` writes the logger's level, timestamp, module, action and message;
context is printed when enabled. Leave PM2's `time` disabled and omit
`log_date_format` to avoid duplicate timestamps. Preserve the generated
`merge_logs: false` when worker separation matters. For structured persistent
entries, configure `JSONFileLog` with a distinct storage path per worker; its
JSON format is independent of PM2's JSON envelope. PM2 JSON logging wraps
captured text, not the logger's original fields. See
[PM2 log management](https://pm2.keymetrics.io/docs/usage/log-management/) and
[Logging](../digging-deeper/logging.md).
